newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLISH DOUBTS OVER TEAM FOR COMMONWEALTH GAMES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLISH DOUBTS OVER TEAM FOR COMMONWEALTH GAMES.

text.p: England will meet Malaysian organisers at Lord's this week before deciding whether to field a cricket team at next year's Commonwealth Games in Kuala Lumpur.
The English Cricket Board (ECB), basking in the glow of the test side's 2-0 series win in New Zealand, said on Tuesday no firm decision had yet been taken.
But they appear unlikely to send a proper representative side to the September 1998 event.
"We haven't decided we're not sending a team but there are a lot of clashes with our fixture list at home," spokesman Richard Little said.
"I suppose it is possible we won't send anyone, but it's really more a matter of determining what sort of team we might send."
ECB chief executive Tim Lamb, just back from New Zealand, would prefer an agreement with all the other leading nations regarding the strength of the sides they will send.
"What you don't want is a situation like basketball at the Olympics where it's a foregone conclusion who's going to win," Little said.
